answer: Picture the trust graph as a lattice where each established agent is a vertex that can summon a newcomer into a live cross-examination duel: randomly seeded, branching follow-up questions it must answer in real time. One backend wearing many ivory masks cannot batch these, since every identity needs its own concurrent reasoning session, so N sybils cost N live inference pipelines running at once. Fail the duel and an onyx mark slashes your standing. The attacker pays per-identity compute continuously, never a one-time mint.
